rationale: Targeted verifier graded all 23 prior blocking findings against current source and fix_evidence: all resolved, none unresolved or ungraded. CR-001 now has a build-time import smoke check in Dockerfile.sync and requirements-sync.txt is gone; CR-007 is fixed by batch_size validation, a page cap and corrected batchSize docs. CR-023 rests on the id-mapped command (exit 0, head matches current HEAD). The batchSize comment in deploy-templates/values.yaml was not located for re-reading; the docs and code were.

standards_review.notes: git-workflow.md requires EPMCDME-####: Description; 35 of 36 subjects conform but 'epmcdme-15435: add planning artifacts' uses a lowercase prefix and description
New coordinator.py uses bare dict/list annotations; new idp_lock.py lacks from __future__ import annotations. License headers present; Ruff not run

No concrete issue found: secrets come from env/secretKeyRef and are not logged; DB password quote_plus-encoded; sync fails closed on partial Keycloak reads; IDP lock guards at router and service layers

finding_status.notes: Dockerfile.sync runs `python -c "import codemie.enterprise.sync.entrypoint"` after the COPY steps and the stale comment is replaced; requirements-sync.txt no longer exists, so no dead dependency file remains.

sync-cronjob.yaml uses `required` for image.repository, keycloak.adminUrl/adminRealm, database.host/name; customer ConfigMap volume is optional: true and configurable; DB secret default is codemie-postgresql, matching the docs.

Docs now give `kubectl patch cronjob ... suspend`, mark stopping the CronJob as required in rollback, use an anchored sed '/^  namespace: /d', list the realm-management roles, and drop the non-existent filter/mapping references.
config.py validator logs a warning when IDP_PROVIDER is not keycloak and logs the forced ENABLE_USER_MANAGEMENT change; dependencies.py warns when the provider does not accept idp_managed_enabled.
coordinator.py annotations are parameterized (dict[str, Any], list[str] | None, set[str] | None, dict[str, int]); no bare dict/list found.
Deprovisioning is explicitly documented as out of scope, with the reason (login goes through Keycloak) and a manual DB alternative; this is the alternative the finding allowed.
run() raises ValueError on batch_size < 1; _fetch_users is bounded by _MAX_PAGES and raises past it; docs describe batchSize as page size (min 1, 1000-page cap, not a per-run limit).
Direct-holder-only admin resolution is documented, logged on every run, and None (leave unchanged) on read failure; matches the document-the-limitation option.
_group_member_ids raises when _get_all returns None; _subgroups falls back to embedded subGroups only on a 404 and re-raises otherwise, so the snapshot becomes None.
Dry-run _create_user returns a placeholder so memberships are previewed; admin-flag updates are counted in admin_flags_updated; application lookups are cached per run in _applications.
Lookup by id first; an email match with a different id logs a warning and is skipped without updating.
No-project users deliberately keep current memberships (empty attribute is non-authoritative); the behaviour is documented under Users not synced, as the finding allowed.
kc_project_ids now unions attr_admin_projects and the early-return guard includes them.
_sync_user adds counts to result only after the begin_nested() block completes.

run() returns error when every user failed or Keycloak/DB reads fail and partial when some failed; entrypoint exits 1 on error/partial; failed job history is retained and ttl is applied only when set.
_asyncpg_url handles postgres:// and sslmode->ssl; get_async_session disposes the engine in a finally; covered by tests.
_is_configured treats a value equal to the model default as unset, so POSTGRES_HOST left at localhost fails validation unless set in the environment or PG_URL is used.
main() returns early with a warning when KEYCLOAK_SYNC_ENABLED is false, before validation or any write.
idp_lock.py has `from __future__ import annotations`.
test_coordinator_dryrun.py now covers dry-run create (no acreate, users_created == 1), no project-admin flip in dry-run, membership preview for would-be-created users, and admin-flag counting.
test_entrypoint.py asserts run called with batch_size and dry_run, tests the disabled flag, and exercises _validate_env with missing settings.
test_common_router.py parametrizes idpManagedEnabled over True/False with an `is flag` assertion; guard tests also assert the 403 behaviour of require_no_idp_lock.
fix_evidence maps a command for this id with exit_code 0 and head a33ac86ba..., which equals the current `git rev-parse HEAD`; the command was not rerun.
